summary: The source permits at most 50 nodes across both lists, which is too narrow for honest runtime scaling, while alternating sorted inputs impose a matching linear worst-case lower bound.

optimality.argument: For two lists whose values alternate until one final node remains, a correct merge must inspect successive heads and link each of the first N - 1 output nodes, giving an Omega(N) worst-case lower bound. The iterative two-pointer merge selects each node at most once and attaches the last sorted suffix directly, so its upper bound is O(N).

replacement_checks.evidence: Alternating values prevent either input from being attached early, so every output choice except the final remaining node requires another head comparison and link update.
Both source pointers move monotonically, each selected node is linked once, and an exhausted source causes the other suffix to be attached in one operation.

Sorted-concatenation oracle tests cover all small non-decreasing lists over a five-value alphabet plus every legal split of the 50-node combined boundary, against both app-local and immutable native sources.
